title: Choose Fender's workbench composition
question: Which layout should carry the Engineer's Job Docket into the real product? Use steer if you want to combine specific parts.

options.label: Centered Docket
options.lineage: A dominant task sheet with a quiet session index and attached evidence slips
options.thesis: The current task owns the center while every earned proof remains visible at its edge.
options.viewport: A narrow left context rail, dominant center docket, right evidence slips, and an integrated bottom composer.
options.risk: The permanent three-column frame can make a fresh session feel busier than necessary.
options.case: Best at scanning active work and proof together; weakest when nothing has happened yet.

options.label: Progressive Casefile
options.lineage: One focused task sheet that unfolds only as the run creates new states
options.thesis: Fender stays nearly empty at the start, then turns one task into a legible engineering record.
options.viewport: A single centered casefile with a large task entry and progressively disclosed objective, work, files, checks, holds, and handoff.
options.risk: Important proof may require scrolling unless completion earns a stronger summary treatment.
options.case: Strongest expression of simple first, informative when needed; it benefits from the Review Desk's completion handoff.

options.label: Review Desk
options.lineage: A central work docket with an on-demand proof lane and signed completion band
options.thesis: Work stays central; proof occupies its own lane only when Fender has something real to show.
options.viewport: A task surface beside an earned proof lane, with a full-width completion handoff at the bottom.
options.risk: A visible session rail and empty proof lane would clutter the new-session state if implemented literally.
options.case: Best completion moment and expert inspection; should not expose all surrounding structure before it is useful.
